title: Relative diagonals of morphisms from DM stacks are locally quasi-finite
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. An etale chart is a representable-by-algebraic-spaces etale map from a scheme, and an atlas is a surjective chart; etale and smooth are tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For every morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$, its relative diagonal $\Delta_f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is locally quasi-finite as a morphism representable by algebraic spaces: for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ and every etale scheme chart $A\to T\times_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X}\mathcal X$, the scheme map $A\to T$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. No local finite-type, separation or representability assumption on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 050N (lemma-separated-implies-morphism-separated), parts (2) and (6): a DM source is quasi-DM and any morphism from it is quasi-DM, i.e. has locally quasi-finite relative diagonal.

proof.text: Fix a scheme test $t:T\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, given by $x,y\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $\alpha:f(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}f(y)$. Put $I=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X,T}(x,y)$ and $J=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y,T}(f(x),f(y))$. The cited Isom-space theorem, applied separately to the two DM stacks, represents both by algebraic spaces over $T$ and makes $p:I\to T$ and $q:J\to T$ unramified. Applying $f$ to isomorphisms defines a $T$-map $\phi:I\to J$, with $q\phi=p$; restriction commutes with this map because $f$ is a morphism of fibred groupoids. The chosen $\alpha$ is a section $a:T\to J$.

source.place: Tag 050N (lemma-separated-implies-morphism-separated), DM case; Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM); Tag 04XS (lemma-properties-diagonal), equation-diagonal

proof.text: Regard $T$ as its representable algebraic space [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Form the algebraic space $P=I\times_{J,\phi,a}T$ using the fibre-product theorem. On every $v:T\!\,{}^{\prime}\to T$, its points are exactly isomorphisms $\beta:v^*x\xrightarrow{\sim}v^*y$ with $f(\beta)=v^*\alpha$. This also describes the 2-pullback of $\Delta_f$ along $t$: its objects are $(z,u:z\xrightarrow{\sim}v^*x,w:z\xrightarrow{\sim}v^*y)$ with $f(w)=v^*\alpha\circ f(u)$. Send this object to $wu^{-1}$; an inverse sends $\beta$ to $(v^*x,1,\beta)$. The arrow $u$ identifies each original object with this inverse image, and an arrow between two triples is uniquely determined by its compatibility with $u$ and $w$. Thus the pullback is equivalent to the discrete sheaf $P$, naturally in $T\!\,{}^{\prime}$. Since $t$ was arbitrary, this proves representability of $\Delta_f$ by algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 04XS (lemma-properties-diagonal), equation-diagonal; algebraic.tex Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal); spaces.tex Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces)

proof.text: Apply unramified cancellation for algebraic spaces to $I\xrightarrow{\phi}J\xrightarrow{q}T$: its composite is the unramified map $p$, so $\phi$ is unramified, with no condition required on $q$. Its base change along $a:T\to J$ is $P\to T$, hence this map is unramified too. These applications impose no local finite-type or representability hypothesis on the original $f$.

For every etale scheme chart $A\to P$, the scheme composite $A\to T$ is unramified by the chartwise meaning of the conclusion in step 3. The scheme unramified-quasi-finite theorem gives quasi-finiteness at every point of $A$, hence local quasi-finiteness in exactly the stated sense. This applies to every scheme test $T$ and every chart, including charts that are not surjective. Together with step 2 it proves the assertion.
